paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God never meant for one person to carry everything alone. Moses, Israel's leader, says it plainly: "I cannot carry the burden for you alone." (Deuteronomy 1:9) And he asks, "But how can I bear your troubles, burdens, and disputes all by myself?" (Deuteronomy 1:12) If the man who spoke with God admits that, you are allowed to say it too, and I'm saying it with my WHOLE mustache.

So Moses shares the load, and the people choose "wise, understanding, and respected men" for him to appoint (Deuteronomy 1:13). Then he charges the judges: "Show no partiality in judging; hear both small and great alike." (Deuteronomy 1:17) Notice the reason he gives: "Do not be intimidated by anyone, for judgment belongs to God." (Deuteronomy 1:17) Leaders get to serve, but the final word is never theirs.

Here's why it matters to you, baker. When you're stretched thin, you can ask for help and share the work, and that is wisdom, not weakness. When you're the one trusted with a job, big or small, you do it fairly, because God is the One who judges. And this is only the start of Moses' sermon, so keep your oven warm, because there's more coming.
